subject: Learning Methods
title: Sleep Loss and Emotional Memory
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sleep Loss and Emotional Memory.

hook.text: Sleep-deprived students remembered 40 % more negative events but forgot 60 % of positive ones.

buildup.text: The amygdala becomes hyperactive without sleep, amplifying negative emotional responses. Positive encoding weakens.

discovery.text: This negativity bias under sleep loss distorts learning. You remember threats and failures but forget successes.

twist.text: REM sleep normally processes and detoxifies emotional memories. Without REM, the emotional charge stays raw.

climax.text: If you're feeling negative about your learning, check your sleep first. Restoring it may fix the emotional bias, not.

punchline.text: Tired brains see darkness. Sleep restores the full picture.

quiz.question: How does sleep deprivation affect emotional memory?
options: All emotional memories are erased equally
Negative memories are preserved while positive ones are forgotten
Emotional memories become stronger in all categories
